problem: Existing collaborative long-horizon VLN benchmarks (CoNavBench) do not enforce strictly synchronized dual-robot rollout on a shared timeline, and their coordination policies are static, unable to adapt when new cross-agent evidence appears. Room-type labels in prior datasets are also noisy or missing.
motivation: Multi-robot relay tasks need robots to hand off and rendezvous, and interaction effects are under-estimated when rollouts are asynchronous. Fixed role schedules fail when a robot finds a target early, gets delayed messages or hits a blocked route, so online reassignment via communication is needed.
key_idea: Decentralized robots exchange compact semantic packets and trigger dialogue only on informative events to dynamically reassign subgoals and replan, all under strictly synchronized dual-robot execution.
insight: Turning on SVB+EDR under the same synchronized protocol raises BSR from 0.15 to 0.22 and SR from 0.32 to 0.39 (ablation table), so gains come from dynamic dialogue-driven coordination rather than the rollout protocol. Benchmark reliability also matters: cascaded VLM plus human verification takes room labels from 92.1% to 100% correctness, versus 68% for CoNavBench.
method: Semantic Visual Bus (SVB): each robot publishes a compact semantic packet (current room, key objects, task-stage, timestamp) to a shared bus B_t={S^1,S^2,anchor memory,roles,dialogue history}; stale partner info falls back to local semantics

Event-driven Dialogue Replanning (EDR): triggers on stage completion, first reliable target discovery, local/partner evidence conflict, or stagnation; does event extraction, filtering, and rewrites the runtime instruction/subgoal priority and relay roles

Synchronous Parallel Execution (SPE): shared world clock; each robot infers its action independently and both are committed simultaneously; bounded freshness window for partner messages in real deployment
RTSA: room-type labels via rule-based keywords, GPT-5.2 and Qwen3-VL-235B panoramic classification with majority vote, then manual review
TriGate: verifies candidate stop points via GT semantic visibility, room consistency, and HM3D-finetuned EVA-CLIP recognizability
ROVE: cascaded episode generation with stop-level adaptive resampling, producing DeCoNavBench (1,213 tasks, 176 HM3D scenes)

setting.backbone: Trained navigation policy (details unspecified; prompt-based context with semantic partner hints), one DeCoNav-trained model vs a CoNavBench-trained baseline
setting.training_data: DeCoNavBench training split (held-out test split); scale not specified
setting.observation: RGB-D (3 RGB + 3 depth views per step per robot), plus partner semantic packets
setting.action_space: low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left 15°, turn_right 15°, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat with HM3D scenes (Fetch and Spot robots); real Unitree humanoids for the real-world demo
setting.privileged: none stated at test time (GT semantics used only for offline benchmark verification)

numbers.extra: held-out test split of DeCoNavBench; SR/ISR/SPL are per-robot, BSR is both-success rate
numbers.evidence: Table 'Comparison between CoNavBench and DeCoNav on the same test split': DeCoNav (Ours) 0.39 0.22 0.47 0.32 4.75

numbers.backbone: same model with dialogue-semantic updates disabled
numbers.evidence: Table 'Ablation of DeCoNav on the same test split': w/o DeCoNav 0.32 0.15 0.41 0.24 4.93

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own DeCoNavBench test split (size not stated); no standard benchmark results. The abstract's 69.2% BSR improvement corresponds to 0.13→0.22.
results: On DeCoNavBench, DeCoNav reaches SR 0.39 / BSR 0.22 / SPL 0.32 / NE 4.75 versus the CoNavBench-trained baseline's 0.28 / 0.13 / 0.18 / 5.19. The ablation shows SVB+EDR adds +0.07 SR and +0.07 BSR over the static variant. A real-robot demo on two Unitree humanoids shows a subtask swap after a blocked corridor.
limitations: Only one baseline (CoNavBench) and a single-dataset evaluation; no comparison with other multi-robot methods, and the training details and the size of the test split are not given
Real-robot evidence is a single qualitative case; the method is limited to two robots and relay tasks
The event triggers and policy-context rewrite are described at a high level, with no ablation of individual triggers or of SVB versus EDR
